transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been getting out of breath when I climb the stairs. It's been bothering me enough that I thought I should get it looked at.
When did you first notice it?
Just since last week, I think.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It comes on when I'm going up the stairs or walking uphill, and it settles down after I rest for two or three minutes.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?

I just get out of breath and have to stop and catch it. It's got to the point where I have to stop halfway up the stairs — there are fourteen of them — and I used to manage it without stopping at all.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's just my breathing — feels like it's in my chest, I suppose. It doesn't spread anywhere or go down my arm or anything like that. No pain with it.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I'm not sure about numbers, but it's bad enough that I have to stop halfway up the stairs to get my breath back. I never used to have to do that.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
Only when I exert myself. I'm not breathless when I'm sitting or resting — it's the stairs and walking uphill that bring it on.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
Well, my ankles get a bit puffy in the evening, and I've started using two pillows at night instead of one. But no chest pain, and I haven't been coughing anything up or had a fever.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've had a heart condition — atrial fibrillation, for about five years now. And I had a heart attack about twelve years ago.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?
I take a blood thinner, rivaroxaban, 15 mg once a day with my evening meal. And bisoprolol, 5 mg once a day. Atorvastatin, 40 mg at night. And ramipril, 2.5 mg once a day.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, I'm not allergic to any medicines that I know of.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Yes, it has. Our bedroom is upstairs, and I'm worried about managing the stairs to get to bed at night. That's really what's on my mind — I'd like to know whether my heart is getting worse.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes, the main thing is I'm worried about getting up and down the stairs to bed, and I'd like to know whether my heart is getting worse.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
